idee_recherchee.texte: Time passes more slowly for an astronaut orbiting Earth or for a clock near a massive object than for someone far from gravity, an effect called time dilation that has been measured with atomic clocks and must be corrected in GPS satellites.

titre: NASA on asteroid size and why impact is a low worry
resume: NASA says an asteroid of about 1 km or more is needed for massive damage and sees no such object likely to hit in several hundred years. Some scientists note a life-ending impact every 60 million years or so, and the 2019 OK asteroid passed within 40,000 miles unseen, but asteroid impact ranks at the bottom of the worry list.
